title: Aim a prequestion at the main goal
statement: A question asked before reading helps learners learn what it asks about and little else, so aim it at the lesson's most important goal.
example: In one meta-analysis, questions asked before study had an effect size of .66 on the information they asked about and .01 on other information.
detail: A research-boundary review checked the primary sources an outside review cited (`grade3-reading/artifacts/feedback-devfactory-2026-09-10/analysis-current-courses/RESEARCH-BOUNDARIES.md`, section 3). The publisher confirms g=.66 for prequestioned information and g=.01 for other information (King-Shepard et al. 2025, https://doi.org/10.1007/s10648-025-10075-7), and a second meta-analysis confirms g=.54 targeted and .04 general (k97/91), with corrective feedback in the pre-study phase excluded (St. Hilaire, Chan & Ahn 2024, https://doi.org/10.3758/s13423-023-02353-8). The review's design conclusion is to target an important learning goal and resource other goals separately.
against: The child-specific targeted estimate was .22 against adults' .62, from few child effects (k20), and the general effect's confidence interval includes zero; the review warns against predicting a .66 effect for Grade 3, and notes that giving answers adds a learning opportunity of its own (the same file, lines 37-43).

evidence.quote: The publisher confirms **g=.66 for prequestioned information and g=.01 for other information**
The **g=.54 targeted / .04 general** estimates are confirmed (k97/91).
**Design conclusion:** target an important learning goal and resource other goals separately.
